root_idea.summary: The root centers on purity, holiness, and removal from impurity or imperfection.
root_idea.development: Its meanings extend from becoming or making pure to sanctification, sacred places, the Holy Spirit, and the divine epithet denoting transcendent purity.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The feminine passive-participle form is an inflection of the same adjective cited under the normalized masculine headword مُقَدَّس.

senses.definition: To purify or sanctify a person or thing in a spiritual or devotional sense.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ, this is explained as purifying oneself and those who obey God for Him; the purification is distinguished from merely removing perceptible filth.

senses.definition: To declare God holy, affirming that He is free from impurity, evil, or imperfection.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative explanation of وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ: declaring God to be holy and free from anything derogatory to His glory.

senses.definition: Hallowed, sacred, or purified from spiritual impurity; consecrated.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of sacred places, including the holy land and the sacred valley; in the Quran-focused explanation, purification concerns spiritual impurity such as associationism rather than merely physical dirt.

senses.definition: The Holy Spirit; in the Quranic usage, the spirit identified with Gabriel and associated with conveying divine purification, revelation, or guidance.
senses.usage_conditions: All supplied Quran occurrences are in the construction رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ. The Quran-focused interpretation identifies the referent with Gabriel; classical discussion also records the Spirit of Jesus, the Gospel, the divine name, or divine protection and guidance as alternative explanations of the expression.

senses.definition: The All-Holy or utterly pure one, free from every imperfection and anything derogatory to divine glory.
senses.usage_conditions: A divine epithet with an intensive sense of holiness, purity, and perfection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go far away into the land or country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I usage describing departure deep into a land or country.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become holy or pure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a thing; it may also be applied emphatically to God in the sense of holiness.
A classical Form II usage, including in expressions invoking or denying divine blessing.
A nominal use referring to the act of praying that a blessing be granted to someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go or come to Jerusalem, Bayt al-Maqdis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II directional usage, comparable to verbs formed from place-names.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hallowed, sanctified, or purified; to be free from impurity or imperfection; or to purify oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage, including descriptions of God as free from every impurity or defect and of a person or thing as becoming purified.
A noun and verbal noun referring to the state or quality of holiness and purity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Enclosure of Holiness, identified with Paradise.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical nominal sense distinct from holiness or purity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Jerusalem, especially in the designations al-Quds and Bayt al-Maqdis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-name meaning the hallowed or consecrated dwelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Holy Land, a designation variously applied to Damascus, Palestine, part of the Jordan region, or Syria.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical geographical designation whose precise territorial reference varies among authorities.
A broader classical extension of the passive participle beyond the Quranic sense of being hallowed or purified.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Blessed or greatly blessed one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical divine epithet emphasizing blessing in addition to holiness and purity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A religious person associated with pilgrimage to Jerusalem, especially a Christian monk; in some usages, a Christian or Jew, or a learned Jew.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized personal noun connected with coming from or going to Bayt al-Maqdis and seeking blessing from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Jerusalem-related or belonging to Jerusalem; as a personal designation, a Jew associated with Jerusalem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective and corresponding personal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel like a bucket or tub.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Hijazi dialectal term for a vessel used for purification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An earthen or wooden pot attached to a water-wheel.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Hallowing or sanctifying is covered by the Quranic purify-or-sanctify sense.
Declaring God free from impurity or imperfection is covered by the Quranic declaration-of-holiness sense.
The Quranic Holy Spirit construction and its recorded referential interpretations are covered there.
Pointer-only entry referring throughout to قُدْسٌ.
Pointer-only entry referring to the separate article for hadith.
The Quranic sacred-land use and the broader regional designation are both represented.

cautions: All supplied Quran occurrences of قُدُس are in the construction رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ; the referent is interpreted as Gabriel in the Quran-focused evidence, while classical interpretations vary.
The classical geographical scope of الْأَرْضُ الْمُقَدَّسَةُ is reported with differing identifications, including Palestine, Damascus, part of Jordan, and Syria.
